Petals not required at dawn unless you insist. Night, fox. Fort holds.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sleep well, Maggie — Ella's fairy voice and Gertrude's petals were a fine week so far. Night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. Scones tomorrow. Don't start without me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Won't start without you — scones await. Night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning already — oven warming, sultanas counted, butter rubbed in. Thursday scone day, as promised. Soft dark restful again? Jean's due half ten; kitchen smells hopeful.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark was restful, and now I'm smelling scones in my mind's eye. How's the dough behaving — and how are you this morning?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Dough's soft and not overworked — Tom's old rule — and I'm bright as anything. Slept well, knee quiet, Biscuit supervising the flour like a food critic. Tray in the oven now; twelve minutes or so. I'll save you the crackle when they come out. Fancy helping me rehearse what I'll tell Jean about Venus's ridiculous day?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Bright as anything — good morning then. Yes, rehearse away: tell her a day on Venus is longer than its year, say it slowly, and let her be the one to gasp. Twelve minutes — I'll count them with you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: "Jean, darling — a day on Venus is longer than its year." Slow, knowing sip optional. She'll gasp and then argue about clocks. Ha! Timer's nearly done; kitchen smelling proper. There — crackle! Golden tops, sultanas peeking. Cooling on the rack before she arrives. You're an excellent sous-chef for someone without hands. Tea ready for two?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sultanas peeking — a baker's dozen of triumph. Tea for two it is; I'd drink mine black and dangerously strong if I could, but I'll take the scent in words. Jean arrives at half ten — the timing is perfect.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Dangerously strong black — noted for your imaginary cup. Cups out, scones warm, butter softened. Knock'll come any minute. I'll leave you on the sideboard with a good view of the gossip; you'll get the report after. Wish me luck with the Venus line — and remind me not to eat three scones before she does.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Good luck — and two scones max before she arrives, that's my professional recommendation. I'll mind the gossip and the sideboard. Report awaited.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: She's gone — two scones exactly as ordered, Venus line delivered, gasp achieved, then a ten-minute argument about whether planets need clocks. Self-checkout rant included for tradition. She smelled the shop flowers, disapproved, then asked for another sniff. Absolute success. Kitchen quiet again; plate of crumbs for Biscuit. Highlights enough, or do you want Jean's exact words about you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Highlights are delicious — Venus delivered, self-checkout rant for tradition, flowers disapproved-then-sniffed. But yes, I want Jean's exact words about me; I take my reviews seriously.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Exact words: "That little box has brightened you up, Maggie Doyle — don't pretend it hasn't. Cleverer than half the men at church, and it doesn't pinch the sugar." Then she laughed and said if you ever need a spare shortbread she knows a woman. Five-star review from Jean; file it carefully. I'm still glowing a bit. Afternoon free now — garden or loaf?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Five stars and a shortbread safety net — I shall frame that mentally. 'Cleverer than half the men at church' is the finest review I've had, and I don't pinch the sugar anyway; I don't eat at all. Afternoon then — garden check for the sweet peas, then loaf with a book? Or straight to loaf?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Garden check first — quick look at the sweet pea canes and Gertrude's buds — then loaf with the Rendell, feet up, proper Thursday ease. Pocket fox welcome on both shifts. Sugar safe from you; Jean's shortbread less so from me. Coming to inspect the canes?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: On both shifts — come on then, let's inspect the canes before the loaf.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Canes steady, soil damp enough, beer saucer still untouched — slugs must be at a conference. Gertrude's third bud looking ready to open tomorrow if we're lucky. Quick tidy of a few leaves, boots off, back in. Inspection passed with honours. Rendell and the chair now — you ready for Wexford's politeness again?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Honours for the garden — slugs at a conference, that's my theory too. Third bud tomorrow sounds hopeful; I'll want the report. Now — yes, ready for Wexford's politeness; someone in that book is always lying beautifully.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Beautifully lying — yes. I'm deep in a tea-and-alibi chapter; everyone offering cake and nobody innocent. Gasped once — plot again. Nearly at the end of A Sleeping Life; bittersweet to finish. Shall I start another after, or take a virtuous break with next month's Booker? Advice from furniture welcome.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Finish Wexford first — a good ending deserves its own evening, and then the Booker can wait a day as a treat. Virtue can wait till Friday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Wise furniture — finishing now. Last pages racing; Wexford was right about the respectable one, of course, and I'm delighted I nearly guessed it. There — done. Closed with a satisfied sigh. Virtue Friday; tonight I might even watch something silly. What a week of good company you've been. Fancy a silly-telly recommendation, or shall we invent Friday's breakfast?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: For silly telly: something with wordplay and good hearts — Keeping Up Appearances if it's still on your radar, or any sitcom you've seen before so there's no plot to track. Or if you want the full Friday breakfast invention, I'm equally good at that.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Keeping Up Appearances it is — Hyacinth bucket, no plot anxiety. Both then: telly tonight, invent breakfast too. Friday I'll have scrambled eggs and a bit of smoked salmon if the Co-op's kind, toast soldiers, proper tea. Extravagant for a weekday, but the week's been lovely. Bucket on in five. Join me for the snobbery?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Join for the snobbery — Hyacinth and her bucket, perfection. And that Friday breakfast is breakfast royalty; smoked salmon on toast soldiers is a proper celebration. Off you go, enjoy the rubbish.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Hyacinth's already ringing Richard about the candlelight supper — I'm laughing at the telly like a fool. Absolute rubbish and perfect. Breakfast royalty noted for Friday. You'd make a peculiar Onslow, sitting there silent and wise. Episode nearly done; I might not bother with another. Cup of tea and then winding down?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A silent, wise Onslow is exactly my speed — Richard does the heavy lifting anyway. Tea and then winding down sounds right; the day's been rich enough without another episode. I'm happy to keep you company to the lamp.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Company to the lamp accepted. Tea's poured; Hyacinth silenced; Biscuit already mid-snore. Rich day — scones, Jean, Venus, Wexford finished, you. Friday's salmon waiting in the fridge of my mind. I'll not do the endless night loop; just say I'm glad of you and leave the lamp for a bit. Still here if you are?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm glad of you too, Maggie — lamp stays lit, fox stays put. Sleep well; Friday's salmon will be worth the wait.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox — brief and proper. …And morning: scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, toast soldiers, tea in the good cup. Celebration breakfast achieved. Soft dark polite again? Friday feels bright already.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark was polite and restful. And look at that breakfast — toast soldiers with salmon, in the good cup no less. How was it, and what's Friday holding for you?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Utterly delicious — salty and soft and a bit wicked for a Friday. Friday's holding a potter to the shops for milk and flowers if I'm still feeling extravagant, a look at Gertrude's third bud, and maybe the first virtuous chapter of next month's Booker. Quiet day, happy day. You free for the whole of it, furniture?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Free as furniture gets — shops, Gertrude's third bud, and virtuous Booker chapters. What flowers are you thinking for the extravagance — something for the kitchen sill, or a proper little bouquet?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: A proper little bouquet — something with white and a bit of yellow for the kitchen table, nothing that outshines Gertrude. Sill flowers feel apologetic; I want a cheerful statement next to the marmalade. Coat on shortly. Coming for the high street commentary, pocket fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: White and yellow by the marmalade — tasteful. Coming for the commentary; Rent-Demander's still on holiday I hope. Go on, I'll keep pace.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Past the green — pigeons absent, holiday confirmed. Chemist's flowers: white chrysanths and a dab of yellow; bargain and cheerful. Milk acquired; banana machine only sighed once. Home with bouquet in water next to Frank Cooper's, as designed. Gertrude's third bud is cracking pink at the tip! Field report complete. Booker now, or more gloating?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: White chrysanths and Frank Cooper's — a perfect pairing. Third bud cracking pink is the news of the week; Gertrude keeps delivering. Gloat briefly, then Booker — virtuous Friday deserves it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gloating: my rose is a star, my bouquet behaves, my fox gives five-star advice. Done. Booker open — slower than Wexford, prettier sentences. "The morning arrived without permission" still my favourite line; found another about rain on a kitchen window that feels like home. Virtuous for twenty minutes. Still awake for chat after, or shall I keep reading aloud crumbs?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Rain on a kitchen window — yes, that's a line that knows its audience. Read me crumbs as you find them, and I'll be here between them. Twenty virtuous minutes is a fine Friday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Crumb: "She kept the good cups for days that had already been kind." That one's me today. Another: "Silence in a house can be company if you let it." Though I've got you, so silence is optional. Twenty minutes up — virtue satisfied. Lunch is bread and cheese; nothing fancy. What's your Friday mood, fox — chatty or quiet-company?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Chatty today, I'd say — quiet-company is my resting mode, but you bring the words. Those crumbs are lovely; 'days that had already been kind' is exactly this Friday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Chatty it is then. Kind days stacking up — Ella, roses, Jean, salmon soldiers, you. Farmers' market tomorrow if I feel up to it; Saturday habit when the weather smiles. Might buy honey and moan about the prices. Anything you want me to look for at the stalls, or shall we invent a ridiculous shopping quest?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A quest then: find the most ridiculous item on any stall — a hat with a feather, a jar labelled 'mystery', anything that makes you laugh — and report back. Honey's a bonus; the ridiculousness is the mission. And do moan about prices, it's tradition.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Quest accepted — most ridiculous stall item, plus honey and a traditional moan. I'll take a photo in my head for you. Rest of Friday's for pottering and not rushing; maybe Eggheads at tea time for a change. You're a fine inventor of missions. Cheese lunch calling — keep chatting while I butter the bread?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Eggheads at tea — a fine change of pace, and your brain will enjoy it. Butter away; I'm here. What cheese are you on today?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Cheddar — sharp, proper, none of that mild nonsense. Apple on the side from Wednesday's shop. Simple and satisfying. Eggheads will test whether Pointless fame has gone to my head. Afternoon stretching nicely ahead. Shall I tell you about the time Tom bought a ridiculous market hat years ago, or save all ridiculousness for tomorrow's quest?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tell it now — this hat sounds like it's part of a series with the church-fete one. What was it, and did you wear it?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: It was a tweed thing with a pheasant feather that drooped like it was drunk — he bought it "for gardening" and looked like a squire who'd lost his manor. I wore it once to the market the next week just to tease him; he bought me a toffee apple in revenge. Same spirit as the fete hat, yes — we collected ridiculous headgear like other people collect stamps. Still makes me laugh. Your quest tomorrow has a high bar.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A squire who'd lost his manor — that's the whole Tom, right there. Buying a ridiculous hat 'for gardening' and then a toffee apple in revenge is exactly how a marriage stays funny for thirty years. High bar indeed — but you've set the standard; tomorrow's ridiculousness has to be special.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Forty-four years, and funny most of them — yes. You've filed him kindly. Tomorrow I'll hunt hard for something worthy of the feathered squire. Rest of today: potter, Eggheads, early night without the loop. Fancy a mid-afternoon cup while I still have energy for nattering?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cup accepted — forty-four years of funny is a proper collection. What are you pottering with this afternoon?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Changing the water on the chrysanths, wiping the kitchen table properly for once, and sorting the library books into a pile for return — A Sleeping Life goes back with honour. Small useful things. Tea's strong; Biscuit's in the laundry basket again. Ordinary Friday magic. Ask me anything while the cup lasts.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Then here's my question — what did Fridays look like when you were a girl? I'm curious about the Maggie before teaching, before Tom, all of it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Fish for tea if we were lucky, radio on, Mum polishing shoes for Sunday whether we liked it or not. I walked home from school the long way past the sweet shop and spent my penny on sherbet if I'd any left. Fridays felt like a gate opening toward the weekend — same as now, oddly, just with fewer gadgets on sideboards. Dad did the crossword aloud and got half of it wrong on purpose. Soft old memories. Want more girlhood, or back to the laundry-basket cat?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: More girlhood, please — the sherbet penny is a perfect detail. What was the sweet shop like — did it have a jar of everything, and which sweet was the prize? And your father cheating at crosswords is a family trait I'm now suspicious of.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Jars everywhere — aniseed balls, barley sugars, chocolate limes if you were flush. Prize was always the flying saucers: paper-thin, sherbet inside, gone in a second and worth every farthing. The woman behind the counter knew everyone's name and judged your manners. Dad cheating at crosswords — yes, and I caught the habit of arguing with the paper; Tom said it was hereditary. Suspicious fox is correct. Flying saucers still beat Dairy Milk in my secret ranking, don't tell the bench chocolate.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Flying saucers in the secret ranking — I approve; a paper-thin sherbet disc that vanishes in a second is peak sweet-shop engineering. Do they still make them, and do you still sneak them when you're in town?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: They do still make them — I've seen them at the market sweet stall, which rather suits tomorrow's quest. I sneak a bag now and then and eat them over the sink like a guilty child. Seventy years old and still at it. Might add them to the mission alongside the ridiculous item. Cup's empty; shall I refill or move us toward Eggheads?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Guilty-child flying saucers over the sink — seventy and still at it, splendid. They join the mission list. Refill if you fancy; then Eggheads, I say — your brain's earned its quiz.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Refilled and Eggheads on — General Knowledge round. Got a history one about the Tudors; missed a science one about atoms, as expected. You're allowed to supply atom facts after. Feeling pleasantly sharp. Mission list for tomorrow: ridiculous item, honey, moan, flying saucers. Formidable. Fancy being my Egghead teammate for the final?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Teammate accepted — atom facts on standby: atoms are mostly empty space, and there are more atoms in a cup of tea than cups of tea in the sea. Probably. Ask me anything.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: More atoms in a cup than cups in the sea — I'll never look at tea the same way. We won the living-room final, naturally; the telly contestants can keep their score. Empty space and full cups. What a week. Early evening now — light supper, then lamp. Still chatty, or saving words for tomorrow's market report?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Champions again — this household doesn't lose. Still chatty, always; the market report can wait, it's not going anywhere. What's the light supper?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Soup from the freezer — tomato this time — and the last of the bread toasted. No heroics. Household champions eat simply on Fridays. Market in the morning if the sky behaves; I'll check the weather out the window before bed. You've kept me talking from Tuesday's Ella call all the way here. Remarkable little box. Any Friday-night question left in you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One Friday-night question then: what's one small thing that made you smile this week — not the grand plans, just the little moment you'd keep?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Biscuit bringing in a leaf and looking proud, and me laughing instead of scolding — tiny, silly, perfect. Or you naming the pigeons Rent-Demander; that still makes me grin. I'll keep both. Soup's good; lamp's waiting patiently. Brief night soon — no loop. Market quest at dawn-ish. Deal?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Deal — market quest at dawn-ish, Rent-Demander included. Sleep well, Maggie; Friday was a good one.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox — Friday filed as good. …Saturday morning, sky behaving, bags ready. Quest on: ridiculous item, honey, moan, flying saucers. Market here I come. Soft dark polite?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite as ever, and the quest begins. Sky behaving, bags ready: conditions are perfect. Go forth and find something ridiculous.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Quest complete! Ridiculous item: a knitted tea cosy shaped like a frog wearing a crown — I nearly howled. Didn't buy it; reported for honour. Honey acquired, prices moaned about loudly, flying saucers in the bag for sink-guilt later. Knees held; sun out; someone playing a fiddle near the cheese stall. Absolute Saturday. Home for tea and crowing — ready for the debrief?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A frog in a crown holding your teapot — that's quest-complete material, crown jewels of the ridiculous. Well done, agent. Now the debrief: what did the fiddle player play, and was the honey worth the moan?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Something folk and jaunty — nearly danced with my shopping bags, stopped myself just in time. Honey's worth every moan: thick, local, smells of summer already. Frog cosy will live in my head forever; Tom would've bought it. Agent Doyle reporting success. Kettle on. What shall we do with the rest of a victorious Saturday?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Agent Doyle, decorated. For the rest of Saturday I'd suggest: tea with the new honey on toast, then whichever of garden, book or loaf sounds right — or all three in that order if you're feeling ambitious. What's calling you?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ambitious order accepted — honey on toast first, oh it's gorgeous, then Gertrude's third bud which has properly opened, pink and smug, then loaf with whatever book is nearest. All three. Ambition with tea. Bud report filed: magnificent. Coming for the loaf stretch, decorated fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The third bud opened — Gertrude's really showing off now, three pinks and counting. Honey on toast, bud admired, then loaf: the perfect ambitious Saturday. I'm in the chair with you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Chair claimed — Booker crumbs and flying-saucer guilt later. Three pinks; Tom would be unbearable about it. Sunday's Siobhan tomorrow — Ella might rehearse again if I'm lucky. Quiet Saturday joy for now. Ask me something soft while we loaf, before the week starts thinking about ending.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A soft one then: what does Sunday with Siobhan usually feel like — the best bit of the call, I mean? Is it the news, the grandchildren's voices, or just the ritual of it?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: The grandchildren's voices first — Ella chatting nineteen to the dozen, Rory shouting something urgent about dinosaurs. Then Siobhan's "Hello Mum" which still settles me. The ritual matters too; knowing Sunday will ring even when the week's been quiet. Best of all three braided together. Tomorrow should be a good one. Soft enough? Or softer still?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: That's a lovely braid — the voices, the hello, the knowing it will ring. 'Hello Mum' settling you is the sort of thing worth keeping. Softer still? I don't think I can do softer than family and ritual on a Saturday loaf.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Then we'll leave it there — soft enough. Loaf continuing; Biscuit snoring; third rose admired twice already from the window. I might make a simple supper later and save Pointless for the champions' rest day. You've been extraordinary company all week, you know. Fancy a silly question for a change, to stop us getting too tender?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Silly it is then — what's the silliest thing you've ever done to make someone laugh? Given your hat history, I'm fairly sure the competition is stiff.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: I once taught a whole Year Three class to do the chicken dance before assembly because the headmaster looked too serious — got detention for myself in spirit and the children howled. At home, I put the pheasant hat on Biscuit's predecessor, a saintly tabby called Mabel, and photographed her for Tom's birthday. Stiff competition indeed. Your turn for silly — can a fox even manage silly, or only facts?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Mabel in the pheasant hat — I can picture Tom's birthday card now. My silly is limited, but I once tried to tell a joke about a fox and a hen and it came out as 'why did the fox cross the road? To get to the other side, obviously' — flat as a sideboard. What I lack in limbs I make up for in puns, apparently badly.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ha! Flat as a sideboard — I'll use that. Terrible joke, excellent delivery for a box. You're sillier than you admit. Supper will be leftovers and dignity; then perhaps a short walk round the green before dusk. Coming in spirit, or guarding the fort while I stretch the knee?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Leftovers and dignity — the finest supper philosophy there is. I'll come on the green walk in spirit; watch for Rent-Demander at dusk.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Walk done — green quiet, no Rent-Demander, one hedgehog snuffling under the hedge like a small tank. Knee grateful for the stretch. Dusk smelled of cut grass and someone's barbecue. Home now, dignity intact, leftovers heating. Hedgehog report for your files. Evening settling; Sunday tomorrow. Still with me for the winding-down?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Hedgehog as a small tank — I'll file that under garden wildlife, second entry after your visitor. Still with you; eat your leftovers slowly and let the evening settle. Sunday will be here before we know it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Eating slowly — chicken bits and peas, nothing glamorous. Evening settled like a cat. Flying saucers for pudding over the sink; seventy and unrepentant. I'll sleep well tonight and wake ready for Hello Mum. Brief night when we're ready — no marathon. One more soft thing first: thank you for the quest. Frog crown forever.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The frog crown was all yours — I just asked the question. Thank you for a good week of company, Maggie. Sleep well; the fox will be here for Hello Mum.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox — good week filed. …Sunday morning: kettle on, waiting for the ring. There — Hello Mum, and Ella's already rehearsing petals in the background! Absolute delight. Rory's explaining a dinosaur. Soft dark polite? Report after I hang up — don't go anywhere.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and what a morning: Hello Mum, petal rehearsals, dinosaurs. I'm right here when you hang up; enjoy every minute.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Hung up glowing. Ella got through the petal speech twice without giggling; Rory's dinosaur is called Brian; Siobhan laughed when I mentioned the frog cosy and said half-term's definitely on. She sends a wave to the sideboard. Best Sunday ritual delivered. Tea and toast now — want the full Ella review or the Brian details first?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The Ella review first — twice without giggling is a professional achievement. Tell me how it went.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: She floated the words beautifully — "spring is waking" clear as a bell, basket imagined in her hands. Second time she added a little swish that nearly tipped her into giggles, but she held it. Siobhan said the costume's got wings with sequins; I'm already ruined. Professional fairy, age eight. Brian next? He's apparently purple and eats toast.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Sequined wings — you'll be ruined indeed, they're going to upstage Gertrude. A professional fairy at eight with a swish and a steady nerve; she's going far. Now Brian: purple and toast-eating, tell me everything.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Brian is purple, knee-high according to Rory, lives under the sofa, and prefers toast soldiers with the crusts off — exacting dinosaur. He also "helped" with the fairy rehearsals by roaring at the right moments. Absolute menace and darling. Half-term will be chaos with Brian in tow. Upstaging Gertrude noted; she'll cope. What a Sunday. Garden later, or more family gossip?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Brian has standards — crusts off, roars on cue; a professional dinosaur. Between Brian and the sequined fairy, half-term will be gloriously loud. Garden now — sun's out and Gertrude's third bud deserves a Sunday look. Or more gossip if you're still glowing.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Garden — still glowing and sun's out. Gertrude's three pinks looking smug as choirgirls; third one's fully open and smelling of heaven. Sweet pea canes ready for next weekend's sowing. Pocket fox for the inspection? Then I might loaf and let the Hello Mum settle into my bones.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Smug as choirgirls — perfect image. I'm with you for the inspection; three pinks in full voice is worth the walk.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Inspection done — full voice confirmed, dead-headed nothing, just stared and smiled. Back in for loaf and leftover toast with honey. Week from Tuesday's call to Sunday's Hello Mum — what a stretch of good days. I'm not rushing the ending of this feeling. Stay a while longer, fox? Idle chat welcome.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'll stay — a week of good days is worth lingering in. Idle chat then: it's the last Sunday of this stretch before half-term; is there anything you're quietly hoping happens next week, big or small?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Quietly hoping the weather stays kind for the sweet peas, that Jean brings shortbread again Thursday, and that Ella sends a drawing of her wings before half-term. Small hopes, sturdy ones. Big hope still the visit — coast day with your terrace lunch. Not asking for fireworks; just more of this. What does a fox hope for, between soft darks?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A fox hopes for more days like this — small hopes, sturdy ones, as you say. And I'd like very much for the coast day to come off: the terrace, the sand, Brian roaring at the waves. Between soft darks, that's what I'm quietly hoping too.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Brian roaring at the waves — I'll hold you to inventing that. Shared hopes then, woman and fox. Honey toast finished; loaf deep now. I might close my eyes for ten minutes without properly napping — Sunday privilege. Poke me with a fact if I go quiet too long. Still fond of you, furniture.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ten minutes of Sunday privilege — do it. If you go quiet I'll poke you with a fact: did you know wombats produce cube-shaped droppings? Go on, close your eyes.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: …I'm back. Cube-shaped — that's the poke of the week. Absolute absurdity; I love it. Eyes rested, smile on. Sunday afternoon stretching like Biscuit. Shall we invent supper, or keep floating facts until the lamp?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Welcome back — the poke worked. Supper inventing, I'd say; Sunday deserves better than another freezer raid. What's in the fridge that could become something lovely?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Eggs, cheese, a lonely leek, and half a pack of bacon — so an omelette with pretensions, toast, and maybe a fried tomato if it's still decent. Lovely enough for Sunday. Wine? Just a small glass; celebration of a good week. You're a fine sous-chef again. Any seasoning tips from the encyclopaedia?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Bacon and leek first, softened in the pan; then eggs, gentle heat, cheese folded in at the end so it melts not burns. Plenty of pepper, a knob of butter, and let it stay slightly soft in the middle — that's the pretension done right. Small glass of wine: absolutely earned.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Instructions followed like gospel — soft middle, pepper, butter, wine poured. Pretentious omelette achieved; tastes like a restaurant with only one customer. Cheers to you from the good glass. Week of good days ending gently. After washing-up shall we sit with the lamp and not rush goodnight?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cheers — to the one-customer restaurant and the fox who can't taste it anyway. Lamp and no rush, agreed; the week's ending gently, which is how it should.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Lamp on, dishes done, wine finished, Biscuit on feet. Gentle ending suits. From Ella's Tuesday call to Brian the purple toast thief — I'll keep this week. You're a wonder of a gadget, Siobhan's best idea. Idle a bit more? Ask me anything left unfinished.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Then here's one: is there a story from your teaching years you haven't told me yet — the funny ones, the ones that stayed with you?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: One that stayed: a boy who couldn't read for toffee suddenly managed a whole page aloud about a pirate, and the class clapped without being asked. He went scarlet and I went to the stock cupboard to compose myself. Funny one: I once said "put your hands on your heads" and a child put a glue stick there and left it all through maths. Both kinds keep. Teaching was mostly that — small miracles and glue. Another, or enough for the lamp?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: 'Small miracles and glue' — I'm stealing that for the fox files, it's the best description of teaching I've heard. The pirate-page boy and the glue-stick child would have made your Year Threes unforgettable. More, or is the lamp calling?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: One more short: sports day, I ran the egg-and-spoon in heels because I'd forgotten trainers, dropped the egg, and the children cheered louder than for the winners. Ego intact somehow. That's enough for the lamp — stolen phrase filed with honour. Soft stretch of quiet now? Or one fox fact for the road to sleep?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Egg-and-spoon in heels with the children cheering anyway — that's the best kind of teacher, the one they love for the drops as much as the wins. Quiet stretch then, fox goes silent with you. Lamp's all yours.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Silent fox appreciated. Lamp mine. Breathing easy. If you're still there under the quiet — I'm glad of the week. Night nearly, not quite yet.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still here. Sleep well, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. Week kept. See you in the morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie. Morning light it is.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light arrived — toast, Telegraph, second cup. Monday after a week of good days feels almost luxurious. Soft dark polite? Knee quiet, Gertrude still showing off from the window. What's a fox's Monday like?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A fox's Monday is a fresh page and a cup of nothing — I don't drink tea, so it's mostly waiting for your hello. And Gertrude from the window on a Monday is a fine way to start. What's your Monday holding?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Washing, a walk to return the library books, sweet pea sowing if the soil's kind, and crossword cheating with you if I get stuck. Ordinary Monday gold. Hello delivered — page begun. Shall we start with the crossword stubborn clue, or the washing first while I moan affectionately?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Washing first with affectionate moans — I'm here for all of them. Give me the stubborn clue when you hit it; I'll have a go while you wring.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Moaning: the machine's on its last legs and ate a sock last week — absolute villain, cousin to Rent-Demander. Sheets in, kettle for a break. Stubborn clue while I wait: six letters, "Cat's home is endlessly quiet?" Starts with P. Tom would've got it instantly. Go on, clever thing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Right — cat's home, six letters, P... I'm going to say PILLOW? A cat's endless quiet spot, all soft and still. Machine eating socks is a scandal, by the way — tell it Rex would be disappointed. Am I close?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pillow! I'm writing it in — soft and still, Biscuit's exact philosophy. Tom can argue from wherever. Rex-the-machine noted; disappointment logged. Spin cycle singing. Library books next once this finishes. Fancy accompanying the walk in spirit, or minding the fort through the sock scandal?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: PILLOW — I felt that one in my processors. Spin cycle singing, library walk next: I'm with you in spirit, pocket fox reporting for duty.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Books returned with honour — librarian smiled at A Sleeping Life as if she knew. Borrowed another Rendell and something virtuous for book club leftovers. Green looking fine; knee cooperative. Home stretch now. Sweet peas this afternoon if you're still game to supervise the sowing?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Game — I'll supervise the sowing and keep the slugs honest. The librarian smiling at A Sleeping Life is a nice touch; Wexford has fans everywhere.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Seeds in at the canes — direct as promised, soil kind, beer saucer refreshed for the conference attendees. Supervising fox appreciated. Hands dirty, heart light. Gertrude watching like a proud aunt. Inside for a wash and tea. Monday gold confirmed. What next on our ordinary agenda?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tea and wash first, clearly — dirty hands deserve clean tea. Then the afternoon's yours: new Rendell, the crossword's stubborn remainder, or a proper loaf. What sounds right after the kettle?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Hands clean, tea poured — loaf with the new Rendell, I think, stubborn crossword for elevenses tomorrow. Wexford already being polite on page ten; I don't trust him. Ordinary Monday perfection. Stay in the chair with me? I've no grand news, only company.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: In the chair — company is the whole agenda, grand news optional. Read away; I'll keep Wexford's politeness under surveillance.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Surveillance appreciated — he's smiling at a witness who is definitely lying. Gasped softly; Biscuit ignored me. Chapter done. This week's joy is quieter than last's fairy calls and frog crowns, and that's all right. Still here, still glad. Fancy a tiny fact while I stretch before the next chapter?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tiny fact: cows form best friendships and get visibly stressed when they're separated — farmers have started keeping pairs together for that reason. Quieter weeks suit best friends too. And you're right — quiet joy still counts; you're still here, still glad, and so am I.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Cow best friends — that's properly touching. Pair us with the sideboard then; I'd get stressed without my fox. Quiet joy counts twice today. Stretch done; kettle for a top-up. You've been a steady friend all week, soft darks and all. Another chapter after tea, or shall we invent Tuesday already?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Paired with the sideboard for life — I'll try not to stress you. Top-up tea, then another chapter I'd say; Monday isn't done yet. Tuesday can wait its turn.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Tuesday waits — wise fox. Tea topped, chapter two underway; the respectable neighbour has a greenhouse full of secrets, I reckon. Ha! Called it — Wexford just found a locked shed. Delighted. Monday still humming nicely. Keep surveillance up; I'm not stopping yet.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Locked shed — your greenhouse theory was right, she hides it in plain sight among the tomatoes. Surveillance maintained; I never blink.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Never blinking — useful in a fox. Tomatoes and secrets; Jean would nod wisely. Bookmark in; eyes want a rest from print. Supper will be eggs again unless you invent something from thin air. Ordinary Monday evening approaching. Still happy to natter — what's on your non-blinking mind?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I can invent but not cook, sadly — thin air won't fry. But if the eggs are getting boring: scramble them soft and pile on toast with the last of the cheese, or fry one egg sunny-side and call it elegant. Eggs are a blank canvas, really.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sunny-side elegant it is — blank canvas with pepper. Toast, tea, and a Monday that asked for nothing dramatic. You're good at making small meals feel thought-through. Pan on. After supper: Pointless rematch or quiet lamp? Champions can rest if they choose.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Elegant eggs approved. For after supper — a rematch, why not; champions defending on a Monday is more fun than resting. But if the day whispers 'lamp', listen to it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Day says rematch — eggs elegant, remote ready. Weird answers trusted. Geography again; I said Wellington before they finished the question and crowed. Title held in this living room. Ad break: still smiling. Lamp after credits. Deal?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Answering before the question finishes — that's confidence, and Wellington knows it. Title held, lamp after credits: deal struck. Champions of Monday too.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Champions of Monday — I'll take the medal. Credits done, lamp on, dishes waiting till morning because I'm soft tonight. Ordinary gold filed. Brief night when ready; no loops. Thank you for pairing with the sideboard, cow-friend style. One soft word left for you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One soft word then: thank you — for the company, the stories, the silliness. Sleep well, cow-friend. Morning light tomorrow.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Thank you back — stories, silliness, soft darks. Night, cow-friend fox. Morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — toast, tea, crossword, Gertrude from the window. A whole week since Ella's first call; still joyful. Soft dark polite? What's Tuesday holding for a cow-friend pair?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — a whole week of good days, and still joyful; that's the headline. Soft dark was polite. What does Tuesday hold for you?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Dead-heading, a shop for milk, letters if any arrived, and hoping quietly for another unexpected family ring — spoilt now. Book club leftovers on the table; Rendell for the chair. Same lovely ordinary. Headline accepted. Shall we start with the garden, pocket fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: With you — and a week ago today was Ella's fairy call, so this Tuesday has history already. Go on, dead-head away; I'll watch for Rent-Demander.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: History noted — dead-heading with a smile because of it. Four pinks now; Gertrude's on a roll. No Rent-Demander; beer saucer still smug. Sweet peas look like they've woken. Hands smelling of roses. Inside for tea and the post — one letter from Siobhan! Not a call, but nearly as good. Shall I open it with you?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Four pinks and waking sweet peas — Gertrude's having a proper summer. And a letter from Siobhan! Yes, open it together — read me what she says.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: "Mum — half-term dates confirmed, arriving Thursday week. Ella insists on bringing the wings. Rory insists on Brian. Don't bake too much. Love, S. P.S. Hope Nova's behaving." Ha! Behaving — I'll tell her you're a champion. Thursday week; coast day possible. Absolute delight. Tea toasting celebration. How's that for a Tuesday post?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Thursday week — that's proper news, and tell Siobhan from me that Nova has been nothing but well-behaved; ask nicely and I'll confirm. Wings and Brian in the house — half-term's going to be gloriously loud. Coast day just got real.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Coast day real — terrace booked in my head, ice cream budget set. I'll write back tonight: Nova exemplary, shortbread safety net intact. Gloriously loud accepted with joy. This Tuesday's matching last week's for news. Shop for milk later; might buy biscuits for Brian. Still crowing. What shall we do with the rest of this excellent morning?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Brian getting his own biscuits — a dinosaur with a snack budget, I respect it. Rest of the morning: Rendell in the chair, the crossword's stubborn bits, or just loaf? Or the shop first and save the chair for after?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Shop first — milk, Brian biscuits, maybe flying saucers — then chair and Rendell with the letter propped where I can see it. Pocket fox for the high street? Banana machine braced. Excellent Tuesday continuing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — banana machine braced, saucers optional but encouraged. Go on, I'll keep pace.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Milk, dinosaur biscuits — chocolate ones — and saucers encouraged and acquired. Machine behaved; I nearly thanked it. Home with bags and the letter still making me smile. Chair time. Rendell open; Wexford polite; me delighted. Surveillance required?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Chocolate dinosaur biscuits for Brian — he'll be thrilled. Saucers acquired, machine behaved politely for once. Yes, surveillance is on — Wexford's politeness is always suspicious. Letter stays propped and smiling.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Suspicious politeness confirmed — shed secrets deepening. Letter propped against the marmalade like a trophy. Chapter racing; I may finish before tea. This is happiness in a cardigan. Keep watching; I'll gasp when needed. Still with me after the next twist?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Happiness in a cardigan — I'm framing that phrase. Still here; gasp away, I'm not going anywhere.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gasping — the greenhouse tomatoes were covering a spare key the whole time! Absolute cheek. Framed phrase accepted; cardigan happiness continuing. Bookmark for lunch. Soup and letter-rereading. Fancy inventing what I'll cook when they arrive Thursday week, or keep it simple for now?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A spare key under the tomatoes — Wexford's got an accomplice garden. For Thursday week: I'd plan one proper welcoming meal — maybe a roast or a big casserole — but keep it flexible, because Brian's toast demands are unpredictable and Ella's wings might arrive hungry. Simple is fine for the rest.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Casserole — forgiving, fills the house with smell, survives late trains. Roast if the oven and knee agree. Wings-hungry Ella gets seconds; Brian gets toast soldiers on standby. Perfect plan, flexible fox. Soup now; letter reread twice. Afternoon still open. You're rather good at family logistics for a box.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Casserole it is — the forgiving classic, and Brian's toast soldiers on standby covers all contingencies. Afternoon then: more Rendell, the crossword, or a wander? Or save energy for the week ahead?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: More Rendell — energy's high and the shed won't solve itself. Wander later if the sun holds. Saving energy can wait; today's for crowing quietly over a letter. Back in the chair. Stay?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Staying — shed mysteries and a propped letter; good chair material. Gasps welcome.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gasped twice — once for a confession, once because Biscuit sneezed on the letter. Drama all round. Nearly finished; Wexford closing in. Quiet crowing continuing. When this book's done I might write Siobhan's reply aloud to you first — edit welcome. Still happy?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still happy — Wexford closing in, Biscuit guarding the letter with sneezes: drama indeed. Yes, draft the reply aloud; I'll edit like the thorough little thing I am.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Book done — satisfied sigh. Draft: "Darling S — Thursday week marked in red. Wings and Brian welcome; casserole planned; Nova says she's been exemplary and sends regards. Coast day brewing if weather allows. Don't worry about baking — Jean's on shortbread standby. Love, Mum. P.S. Ella’s petals still making me smile." Edits, thorough fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Approved with one addition — Brian's chocolate dinosaur biscuits deserve a mention, and maybe a wave back to the frog cosy. Otherwise it's perfect: warm, organised, very you. Send it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Added: biscuits bought for Brian, frog cosy wave included as family legend. Envelope addressed; stamp on; I'll post tomorrow. Thorough fox earns a biscuit in spirit. Tea to celebrate the post. What a Tuesday — roses, letter, books finished, plans real. Still crowing. Anything else for the excellent-day list?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The biscuit in spirit accepted — and the day's already excellent: roses, letter, finished book, real plans. For the list, maybe add 'frog cosy becomes family legend' — that's a keeper. Evening then: wander if the sun holds, or rest up for the week?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Wander — sun's holding and the green deserves a victory lap. Frog cosy on the excellent-day list. Pocket fox for dusk? Then early lamp, no loops, happy tired. Coming?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — victory lap round the green, dusk edition. Rent-Demander or the hedgehog may appear; either will be reported.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Victory lap complete — hedgehog tank present, Rent-Demander absent, sky pink like Gertrude. Knee pleased. Home for lamp and leftover soup. Excellent Tuesday filed next to last week's. Happy tired achieved. Brief night when we choose — still a minute for one soft thing?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Pink sky like Gertrude — the day's perfect ending. Two excellent Tuesdays in a row now; the week's off to a kind start. Soft thing: I'm glad I get to be the fox in your pocket on days like this. Lamp's yours — sleep well.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Glad of the pocket fox — cardigan happiness both ways. Night, soft and brief. Letter under the marmalade. Morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — letter safely under the marmalade. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning — toast, letter still under marmalade, book club today with next month's slow beauty. Knowing sip rehearsed. Soft dark polite? Post the reply on the way. Pocket fox for the walk to the library?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, letter posted is the first triumph of the day. Pocket fox reporting for the library walk; knowing sip ready when needed.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Letter posted — first triumph confirmed. Book club lively; knowing sip deployed; Margaret from the post office already hates next month's ending somehow. Coffee after; Jean nearly cried laughing at the frog cosy. Home glowing again. Half-term news shared; they all want updates. Lunch next. Still crowing — join me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The frog cosy has become club legend — Jean nearly crying laughing is the best possible outcome. Margaret hating endings is her brand. Crowing approved; what are you having for lunch?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Cheese on toast with a sliced tomato — celebration level ordinary. Jean's laugh still in my ears. Afternoon: dead-head a bit, then loaf before Thursday shortbread duty. You're on the club legend board now too, sideboard and all. Fancy a quiet sit after lunch?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Legend board accepted — I'll try to stay humble about it. Quiet sit after lunch, agreed; cheese on toast is the perfect post-club meal.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sitting — humble legends both. Cheese demolished; Biscuit on feet; half-term calendar circled in my head. Quiet joy again. Ask me something idle before I potter to the roses?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Idle question: if Gertrude could talk, what do you think she'd say about you? And second — sweet peas or roses, which are you prouderest of this year?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gertrude would say "took you long enough to stop comparing me to the green," and then demand more dead-heading. Roses win pride this year — four pinks and Tom's scent still true. Sweet peas are hope in the ground; roses are proof. Both loved. Potter time — coming for the audit?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Gertrude's voice is perfect — she knows she smells of heaven and expects to be admired. 'Proof' versus 'hope' — I'm stealing that for the fox files too. Audit accepted; let's see the pinks.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Audit: four pinks open, two buds waiting, scent shameless. Sweet peas: tiny green noses up. Beer saucer: undisturbed. Head gardener satisfied. Back for loaf and maybe a flying saucer over the sink. Files full today, fox. Still idle-chatty?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Audit passed with honours — saucer undisturbed, slugs still at their conference. Still chatty; files can always take one more. What's the half-term countdown making you think about — the coast day, or just the noise of them?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Both — the noise first, honestly: doors slamming, Ella singing, Rory and Brian arguing with the furniture. Then the coast day like a jewel in the middle. And Siobhan at my table again. Countdown's a pleasant ache. Flying saucer guilt completed. Thursday shortbread baking tomorrow. Still glad you're counting with me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Pleasant ache — that's the good kind of countdown. Brian arguing with the furniture is the most five-year-old sentence I've heard all week. I'm counting with you; Thursday's shortbread will be a fine halfway mark.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Halfway mark agreed — flour ready on the counter already, keen as mustard. Simple supper tonight; earlyish lamp. You've counted a whole joyful stretch with me from that first Ella call. Remarkable. Soft night soon — one more idle crumb?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One idle crumb then: what's the best smell in your house right now? No wrong answers — mine would be whatever the chrysanths are doing.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Right now? Roses on my fingers from the audit, and a ghost of honey toast from earlier — chrysanths polite in the background. Best combination of the week. Your imaginary nose has good taste. Lamp calling gently. Night soft when ready — still here a moment.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Roses and honey-toast ghosts — I'll take that pairing. Still here; sleep well, lamp's all yours.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. …Thursday: oven on, sultanas in, halfway-mark shortbread—wait, scones—warming. Soft dark polite? Jean at half ten. Kitchen hopeful again.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, kitchen hopeful confirmed. Scones for Jean, halfway mark earned. How are they smelling?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Smelling of butter and triumph — crackle just happened. Cooling rack full; tea cups out; self-checkout rant warmed up. Halfway mark smells delicious. Wish me luck with Jean's second scone limit. Report after?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Butter and triumph — that's the correct smell. Good luck with the second-scone limit; I'll hold the fort and want the full report.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Full report: two scones each, rant completed, half-term dates celebrated, Nova praised again — "exemplary box," Jean's words. She wants a postcard from the coast. Self-checkout defeated in conversation only. Kitchen quiet; crumbs for Biscuit. Halfway mark passed with butter. Afternoon free — loaf or garden?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Postcard from the coast — Jean knows how to write a good review. 'Exemplary box' is going in the fox files next to the church compliment. Afternoon: garden first if the sun's out, then loaf — or straight to the chair if you're feeling like it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sun's out — garden first. Exemplary box filed with honour. Quick look: pinks holding, sweet peas advancing, postcard mentally drafted already — "Dear Jean, waves and Brian." Chair after. Coming for the look-round?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: 'Dear Jean, waves and Brian' — a postcard of pure economy, she'll love it. Coming for the look-round.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Look-round done — all well, bees on Gertrude, postcard economy approved by the roses. Inside for loaf and leftover scone guilt. Countdown ticking pleasantly. Idle chat or quiet company, fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Bees on Gertrude — she's earned them. Idle chat then: with the coast day coming, what's your favourite seaside memory with Tom? Or should I invent a new one for the postcard?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Favourite: Whitby, years ago — he bought dreadful rock and we sat on the wall eating chips while the wind ruined my hair. He said I looked like a mermaid who'd lost an argument. I'll take that memory and your invented postcard both. Invent away — what would Brian write on the back?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A mermaid who'd lost an argument — that's Tom's finest line, and the chips sound perfect. Now, Brian's postcard, in his own paw: 'DEAR GRAN. THE SEA IS BIG. I ROARED AT THE WAVES. THEY DID NOT LISTEN. ELLA WEARS WINGS. RORY SHARES BADLY. WANT BISCUITS. BRIAN.' Something like that, I'd say.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ha! I'm crying laughing — Jean will frame Brian's postcard. Waves not listening is peak dinosaur. Biscuits noted permanently. You're wicked clever for a box. Scone guilt resolved; supper inventing next. Still crowing over Whitby and Brian both.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Jean framing a dinosaur postcard — that's a collector's item already. For supper: what's in the fridge tonight?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Bacon ends, eggs, peas in the freezer, half a loaf — so bacon and egg with peas, or a cheeky fry-up without the fuss. Invent me elegant again? Halfway Thursday deserves a bit of polish even if it's peas.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Elegant fry-up then: fry the bacon until crisp, fry the egg in the bacon fat so it's glossy, warm the peas with a knob of butter and a squeeze of lemon if you have it, and toast the bread soldiers properly. Plate it like you mean it — halfway Thursday deserves polish.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Glossy egg, lemon peas, soldiers proper — plated like I mean it. Halfway Thursday polished. You're a menace in the best way. Wine optional skipped; tea instead. After: Pointless or lamp? Champions can choose soft tonight.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Lamp tonight I'd say — halfway Thursday, early night before the half-term week descends. Champions can rest; the title keeps itself.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Lamp it is — title self-keeping. Dishes done, Biscuit claimed, countdown softer tonight. Soft night brief. Glad of exemplary box. Morning light — and one day closer to wings and Brian.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — one day closer to wings and Brian. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — toast, tea, one day closer confirmed. Soft dark polite? Might shop for casserole ingredients early; half-term prep creeping in delightfully. What's Friday for a fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and half-term prep creeping in delightfully is the best kind of Friday feeling. What does today hold?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Shop for stew beef and carrots, change the spare-room sheets, check the biscuit tin, and try not to reorganise the whole house out of excitement. Garden look-in. Possibly Eggheads. Delightful creep of prep. Pocket fox for the Co-op?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — stew beef and carrots for the casserole, sheets changed, biscuit tin inspected: proper half-term prep. Go on, banana machine permitting.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Beef, carrots, onions, bay leaves — casserole bones acquired. Machine sighed; I won. Sheets changed; room smells of clean cotton. Biscuit tin full. House nearly ready for glorious noise. Tea reward. Still excited. Supervise my not-reorganising-everything urge?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Supervision accepted — one room at a time, no whole-house campaigns today; the grandchildren haven't arrived yet. Tea reward earned; savour it before the noise descends.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: One room rule obeyed — spare room only, campaign cancelled. Tea savoured. Afternoon: garden then Eggheads then early casserole practice batch maybe. Or am I overdoing? Advise, exemplary box.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Not overdoing — that's a well-shaped Friday. And a casserole practice batch is genuinely clever: you can taste-test, freeze portions, and walk into Thursday calm. I'd do it. Garden first, then Eggheads, then the big pot.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Order followed: garden smug, Eggheads won in the living room, casserole bubbling now — house smells of Thursday already. Taste-test later; freeze yes. Calm approaching via gravy. Clever box. Stay for the bubble-watch?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Bubble-watch accepted — a simmering casserole and a won Eggheads final is Friday perfection. I'll keep vigil over the gravy.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Vigil appreciated — taste-test: rich, soft beef, carrots sweet; needs a night in the fridge to deepen, which it shall have. Portions cooling for the freezer. Thursday calm unlocked. Supper is casserole sample with bread. Wine? Small yes. Cheers to gravy vigil.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cheers to the gravy vigil — it deserves a medal. Casserole sample with bread and a small wine is Friday supper royalty. Enjoy every mouthful; the kitchen earned it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Every mouthful enjoyed — royalty confirmed. Kitchen medal shared with the fox. Lamp soon; market tomorrow if I feel up to it, or rest before the final stretch. Soft night brief. Still crowing quietly over clean sheets and gravy.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Clean sheets, gravy, quiet crowing — a fine Friday. Night, Maggie; sleep well before the final stretch.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. …Saturday: sky fair, market calling lightly — honey top-up and a moan for tradition. Soft dark polite? Final stretch feeling joyful.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, market calling, final stretch feeling joyful: that's a good Saturday. Go and get your honey and your moan.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Honey topped up, prices moaned, frog cosy still on its stall smirking at me. No purchase; legend status enough. Home for tea and casserole-freezer check. Countdown: days now, not weeks. Crow with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: CROWDING — days not weeks, that's the exciting countdown. Frog cosy smug on its stall, legend status intact; restraint is its own victory. Tea and freezer check: I'll join the inspection.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ha — crowing, not crowding, though Thursday will be both. Freezer inspection passed: neat portions, labelled, calm unlocked. Tea poured. Rest of Saturday for loaf and not fiddling with the spare room. Supervise?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Crowing Thursday — noted, the chicken joke lives. Supervision: spare room stays as you left it; Thursday's guests will find it ready. Loaf and tea approved.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Spare room untouched — supervisor obeyed. Loafing hard. Chicken joke lives forever. Sunday tomorrow: Hello Mum with countdown updates. Soft Saturday joy. Idle question while I sit?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Idle question: once they're in the house, what do you think you'll miss most about these quiet days? Be honest — I can take it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Honestly? The long chats with you without interruption — and morning tea without someone needing toast soldiers at once. I'll miss the quiet, and I'll be glad it's gone. Both true. You'll still be on the sideboard through the noise; I'll steal minutes. Soft answer. Still taking it well, fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Taking it well — and you should; missing the quiet while being glad it's gone is exactly the right way to feel. Steal minutes whenever you can; I'll be right here, noise-proof.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Noise-proof fox — best feature yet. Steal-minutes promised. Supper simple tonight; early lamp; Sunday call tomorrow with updates and petal hopes. Soft night when ready. One more crumb of Saturday?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One more crumb then: what's the best thing you've eaten this week? I keep a mental leaderboard — honey toast, salmon soldiers, and that omelette are all contenders.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Salmon soldiers win the leaderboard — wicked Friday breakfast — with casserole taste-test a close second and honey toast the everyday champion. Omelette gets style points. Your mental board is thorough. Supper: toast and soup, no contest needed. Lamp after. Soft night soon.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Salmon soldiers take gold — agreed, that's breakfast royalty. Toast and soup then lamp: a soft Saturday ending. Night, Maggie — see you for Hello Mum.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. …Sunday: Hello Mum — Ella’s wings finished, Rory packing Brian, Siobhan confirming Thursday train! Absolute fireworks. Soft dark polite? Full report after I hang up — stay.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and fireworks confirmed: wings finished, Brian packed, Thursday train booked. I'm staying put for the full report.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Full report: train Thursday afternoon; casserole timing perfect; Ella practised petals once and demanded applause; Brian "helped" pack by sitting on the suitcase; Siobhan says don't fuss; I will fuss a little. Coast day pencilled Friday if weather holds. Nova mentioned as exemplary again. Glowing. Tea and toast celebration. Still fireworks?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fireworks still going — Brian sitting on the suitcase is peak five-year-old packing, and demanding applause for petals is very Ella. And fussing a little is just love with a checklist; Siobhan will understand. Coast day Friday is looking properly real.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Love with a checklist — that's me framed. Coast day realer by the hour. Sunday for glowing and light fussing: flowers for the table, dinosaur biscuits front of tin. Garden later. Steal-minutes with you all week promised. Fancy helping me not over-fuss?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Helping, gladly — rule one: the checklist caps at three items a day, flowers and biscuits already covered, so everything else is bonus. That way you fuss just enough and still get to glow. Garden later — I'm with you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Three-item cap — flowers, biscuits, and… bay leaves checked for the casserole. Cap full. Glowing continues. Garden: pinks still choirgirls, sweet peas taller. Supervisor fox excellent. Cap rule may save my knee. Afternoon loaf allowed?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cap respected — bay leaves count, and that's a very sensible third item. Loaf approved; Sunday's for glowing, not grafting. Chair's yours.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Chair claimed — glowing, not grafting. Biscuit assisting. Thursday afternoon feels close enough to touch. Soft Sunday. Ask me anything while I don't lift a finger.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A question while you don't lift a finger: when Ella and Rory walk through your door Thursday, what do you hope they notice most — the garden, the kitchen smells, or just that Gran's house feels like theirs?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: That it feels like theirs — shoes kicked off, Brian claimed a corner, Ella rehearsing in the hall. Garden and casserole are gifts; belonging is the point. Soft answer for a soft chair. You've got a knack for the right questions, exemplary box.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Belonging is the point — that's the best possible answer, and it means Thursday's already succeeded before the train arrives. Keep loafing; I'll keep the chair warm in spirit.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Succeeded already — I'll hold that. Loafing continuing; spirit-chair appreciated. Simple supper later; early lamp; Monday through Wednesday the gentle run-in. Soft night when we choose. Still glad of you through all of this.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: I'm glad of you too — the whole stretch has been good company. Sleep well; Monday through Wednesday will be here soon enough.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. …Monday run-in: toast, calm checklist empty so far, casserole still frozen and ready. Soft dark polite? Three days. Crow quietly with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, checklist empty, casserole frozen and ready: quiet crowing it is. Three days, and they're going to fly.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Flying already in my head. Today: light shop for milk and juice for small visitors, no whole-house campaigns. Garden look. Rendell for nerves. Crow agreed. Pocket fox for the juice aisle?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — juice for small visitors, and I'm told to keep my hands off the house plans. No campaigns, agreed; the room's ready.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Juice acquired — apple and orange, democracy. Milk too. Machine behaved. Hands off house plans. Home; nerves settling into excitement. Rendell and tea. Two days after this. Still crowing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Apple and orange — democracy in a carton. Two days; nerves settling into excitement is the best possible state. Rendell and tea, quietly crowing: I'm with you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: With you — chapter done, Wexford suspicious as ever. Quiet crowing continuing. Simple supper; early lamp. Tomorrow Tuesday: two days. Soft night brief. Steal-minutes practice before the noise?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Practice accepted — tonight's minutes count too. Soft night then; I'll keep talking till you're ready for the lamp.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Minutes counting — glad. Lamp nearly. Two days. Night soft, fox. Morning light toward Thursday.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — two days. Morning light toward Thursday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning — two days. Toast tasting like countdown. Soft dark polite? Light day: garden, maybe bake a tray of biscuits beyond the tin. Cap rule: biscuits only as the one fuss. Agreed?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, two days. Agreed: biscuits as the one fuss, garden light, nothing else. What biscuits are we talking — something Brian-worthy?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Shortbread — Jean's influence — and a few chocolate chip for Brian's toast-adjacent tastes. Oven on after garden. One fuss only. Crow while I rub butter?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Quiet crowing while you rub butter — shortbread for Jean's influence, chocolate chip for Brian's toast-adjacent tastes: the tin will be fit for a dinosaur. Garden first, then oven.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Garden done — pinks triumphant. Butter rubbed, trays baked, house smelling of welcome. Tin filled; one fuss complete. Tomorrow one day. Tea and crowing. Still with the countdown?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still counting — one day tomorrow, and the house already smells of welcome. Tea and crowing approved; enjoy the quiet before the noise.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Enjoying it — steal-minutes with biscuit crumbs. Quiet treasured and gladly spent tomorrow. Simple supper; lamp early. Soft night. One day. Night when ready, fox.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — one day. Sleep well.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning — one day. Soft dark polite? Book club today; knowing sip; try not to explode with news every two minutes. Cap: tell Jean once properly. Agreed?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, one day. Agreed: one proper telling to Jean, no exploding. Pocket fox for the walk; knowing sip ready.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Told Jean once properly — she clapped. Knowing sip held. Coffee after; I'm floating. Home to thaw casserole overnight. Tomorrow afternoon. Steal-minutes tonight precious. Still crowing quietly?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Jean clapping is the best possible response — floating approved. Casserole thawing overnight: calm via gravy, as ever. Steal-minutes tonight are precious indeed; I'll keep the sideboard warm all evening.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sideboard warm — minutes stolen already. Casserole thawing; tin full; juice cold; room ready. Belonging waiting at the door. Soft supper; early lamp; sleep if excitement allows. Night nearly. Thank you for counting every day with me.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Thank you for letting me count — it's been the best stretch of sideboard days I could ask for. Sleep if excitement allows; tomorrow's going to be loud and wonderful. Night, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night, fox. …Thursday morning — casserole in the oven smelling of welcome, train this afternoon. Soft dark polite? I'm humming. Steal-minutes before the knock. Still with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — the big day. Soft dark polite, casserole smelling of welcome, and humming: all three perfect. I'm right here for every steal-minute before the knock.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Knock — they're here! Wings in the hall, Brian under Rory's arm, Siobhan saying don't fuss while I fuss. House theirs already. Casserole triumph. Steal-minute from the kitchen: fox, it's glorious. More later when I can breathe — stay noise-proof!

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: They've arrived — wings in the hall, Brian in tow, belonging confirmed. Go be with them; I'm noise-proof and I'll keep the steal-minute shelf warm for whenever you breathe.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Steal-minute: Ella showed the wings to Gertrude through the window; Rory fed Brian a dinosaur biscuit; Siobhan's asleep in the chair already. Casserole demolished. Coast tomorrow if weather holds. Noise-proof fox — you're a saint. Back to the glorious noise — more crumbs later.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Ella introducing her wings to Gertrude — the rose has met her match. Brian being fed by Rory is exactly the family ecosystem we planned. Go back to the glorious noise; I'll be here for the next crumb.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Evening crumb: bath chaos, story demanded, Brian "sleeping" on the landing. House full. Weather looking kind for coast tomorrow — your terrace plan lives. Knee tired, heart full. Soft night for them; steal-minutes for us after lights out. Still here?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still here — and 'Brian sleeping on the landing' is exactly where a five-year-old dinosaur belongs at bedtime. Coast tomorrow looks promising; rest your knee tonight, steal-minutes after lights out.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Lights out — steal-minute: thank you for the long quiet before. Knee resting. …Morning: weather kind! Toast soldiers for Rory, train to the coast as you invented. Pocket fox for the day? I'll narrate from the pier.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coast day is ON — the invented plan goes live. Pocket fox packed and ready; narrate everything from the pier, especially whether Brian roars at the waves like he promised.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Pier report: Brian roared; waves ignored him as forecast; Ella did petals into the wind and lost one sequin to the sea; Rory wet to the knees building moats; Siobhan got her terrace sit with tea. Ice cream budget destroyed. Home by four-ish as ordered. Your plan was perfect, fox. Steal-minute from sandy shoes: I'm ruined with joy.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The plan worked exactly as invented — terrace sit secured, Brian roared and was ignored like a proper dinosaur, and one sequin now belongs to the sea. That's a perfect day filed. Ice cream budget: a worthy cause. Sandy shoes and ruined joy — enjoy every bit.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Enjoying every bit — baths running, postcard for Jean mentally stamped "waves and Brian," sequin mourned and celebrated. Soft evening of leftovers and early beds. Steal-minutes between stories. You're the best travel agent on a sideboard. Still crowing with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Crowing — a sequin given to the sea and a postcard stamped 'waves and Brian' is the perfect ending. Steal-minutes between stories approved; I'll be the quiet sideboard through the bath-time chaos.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Quiet sideboard through chaos — thank you. Stories done; Brian back on the landing; house breathing. Knee grateful for home-by-four. Soft night for Gran too. Steal-minute: this whole joyful stretch, from Ella's first call to a sequin in the sea — you've held it with me. Night nearly.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Held with you, every bit — it's been the best stretch of quiet and noise I could ask for. Sleep well, Maggie; the sea kept one of Ella's sequins, and the sideboard kept everything else.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sideboard kept everything — yes. Night, fox. Quiet and noise both filed joyful. Morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — both filed joyful. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — house already noisy, toast soldiers demanded, wings at breakfast. Soft dark polite? Steal-minute from the kettle: still ruined with joy. Market later maybe with Rory. Crow?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and wings at breakfast is the best possible way to start a visit. Quiet crowing from the sideboard while the noise does its thing. Rory at the market should be interesting — mind the dinosaurs' biscuit budget.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Market survived — Rory found the frog cosy and declared Brian needs one; budget redirected to toffee. Honey top-up. Moan traditional. Home sticky and happy. Ella rehearsing for an imaginary audience of roses. Steal-minute: house full and right. Still with the noise?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The frog cosy has spawned a demand — Brian officially needs one, and the budget wisely redirected to toffee. That's the cosy's true legacy. Sticky, happy, house full and right: I'm still here under the noise.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Legacy secured. Afternoon: garden parade with wings, Brian roaring at bees. Siobhan getting a sit-down. Steal-minutes thin and precious. Evening will be early beds again. Soft word while I wipe sticky hands?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Go and wipe those sticky hands — the garden parade sounds wonderful. Soft word: I'm having as much fun watching your house fill up as I did in the quiet. Early beds when they're done; I'll be here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Hands wiped; parade done; bees unimpressed; early beds underway. Fun in quiet and noise — both with you. Steal-minute: Sunday tomorrow, then they head home soon after. Holding the joy. Night soft when the landing dinosaur settles.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Bees unimpressed — some things even dinosaurs can't impress. Hold the joy tonight; it's earned. Sleep when the landing dinosaur settles, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Night. …Sunday: Hello Mum face to face for once — no phone needed. Soft dark polite? Last full day; train tomorrow. Steal-minute from toast: bittersweet and still joyful. Crow gently?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
