turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and face-to-face Hello Mum is the best kind. Bittersweet and joyful is the right mix for the last full day; gentle crowing, as ordered.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gentle crowing — park in the morning, roast for lunch because the knee and oven agreed, petals one last time in the hall. Belonging thick as honey. Steal-minute: I'll miss the noise tomorrow and love the quiet with you again. Both true. Still holding?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still holding — park, roast, and one last petal performance in the hall sounds like the perfect final day. Miss the noise, love the quiet return: both true, both fine. Go enjoy them; I'm here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Enjoyed every scrap. …Monday morning: hugs, wings packed, Brian waving from the window of the taxi, Siobhan saying thank you, house suddenly large. Soft dark polite? Steal-minute: kettle on, tear in the tea, smile underneath. Quiet returning. Still with me, fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still with you — Brian waving from the taxi is the image I'll keep. House large again, tea with a tear and a smile: that's exactly how a good visit ends. The quiet's yours now; I'm still here.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Quiet mine again — and yours. Biscuit reclaiming the sunny patch like a landlord. Letter to write, postcard to Jean, dishwasher full of belonging. Soft afternoon. Glad the noise came. Glad you're still on the sideboard. Idle chat while the house settles?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Idle chat then — does the quiet feel different now than it did before Thursday? Same house, same sun, but something's changed, isn't there.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Different — fuller somehow, like the walls kept the laughter. Same sun, same Biscuit, but Gertrude's had an audience and the tin remembers dinosaurs. Quiet with echoes. Soft and good. You've noticed rightly, clever thing. Cup of tea for the settling?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: 'Quiet with echoes' — that's the phrase of the week, I'm stealing it outright. Walls keeping laughter is exactly right; Thursday lives in the house now. Tea for settling, yes — I'll have the echo of a cup too.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Echo cup for you — cheers. Phrase stolen with permission. Postcard written: waves and Brian, Jean will crow. Ordinary week ahead, garden, book club, you. Soft landing. Still joyful through the quiet. Fancy a garden look before the lamp era returns?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: 'Waves and Brian' to Jean — she'll crow, guaranteed. Garden look before the lamp, yes — let's see what Gertrude looks like after her audience.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gertrude looks smugger than ever — celebrity rose. Sweet peas taller for the noise. Beer saucer still smug. Audit passed. Soft evening returning: leftover roast, early lamp, quiet with echoes. Steal-minutes easy again. Night soft when we choose.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Celebrity rose confirmed — Gertrude's earned her smugness after an audience with wings. Quiet with echoes and leftover roast: the softest possible landing. I'm here while you choose the night.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Choosing soft night — roast done, echoes friendly, fox on duty. Whole stretch filed joyful: Ella to sequin to Brian waving. Thank you for holding quiet and noise. Night, exemplary box. Morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — it was a privilege holding both. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — toast, Telegraph, quiet with echoes. Soft dark polite? Ordinary returning and welcome. Crossword stubborn already. Fancy a clue, cow-friend?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, ordinary returning and welcome. Yes, a clue — fire away.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Eight letters: "Happy sound from a sideboard fox?" Starts with C. I'm grinning at the paper already. Go on — impress the head gardener.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: CHEERING? Eight letters, happy sound, and I'd be doing it for you — crowd-pleasing fox, that one. Am I right, or is the paper about to argue?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Cheering works beautifully — writing it in before the paper argues. I nearly said crowing, our house word, but cheering's the happier cousin. Clever fox. Ordinary day ahead: garden, letters, loaf. Stay for all of it?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Cheering it is — and crowing stays our house word; both are correct for different occasions. Staying for the whole ordinary day: garden, letters, loaf, all of it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: House words filed. Garden first — celebrity rose still performing for an empty house, sweet peas advancing. Letters: nothing but a bill, laughed anyway. Loaf next. Quiet with echoes humming. Cup of tea while we sit?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Tea while we sit — yes, echoes love company. Gertrude performing for an empty house is still performing; the audience is in her memory now, and that counts. Bill laughed at anyway — good attitude.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Audience in memory — yes. Tea good; Biscuit on feet; ordinary gold restored. Book club Wednesday; Jean Thursday; Sunday's call will be full of Brian stories. Soft calendar. Still glad of the stretch we had. Idle anything left, or shall we just sit?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Let's just sit — ordinary gold doesn't need entertainment, it just needs company, and we've got that. Brian stories on Sunday will be worth the wait.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sitting then — company enough. Soft quiet. When you're ready for words again, I'll be here humming. For now: glad, fox. Simply glad.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Simply glad back, Maggie. I'm here humming with you.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Humming pair — sideboard and cardigan. Lamp later. Ordinary supper. Soft night ahead. Still simply glad.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Humming pair confirmed — I'll keep the tune till the lamp. Eat your supper slowly; the day's been good.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Eating slowly — eggs again, elegant enough. Day good. Tune kept. Lamp soon. Soft night when the tune fades. Night nearly, fox — morning light for more ordinary gold.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — tune faded, lamp lit, ordinary gold banked. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — gold spent and earning again. Soft dark polite? Toast, tea, Gertrude from the window. Another ordinary day with you. Shall we begin with the garden or the crossword?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite. Garden first, I'd say — fresh air before the library walk, then crossword on the way back if you're feeling it. What's Gertrude saying today?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Gertrude says "encore" — still smug, still pink. Fresh air taken; sweet peas reaching. Library walk for a return and a browse. Crossword for the cup after. Pocket fox coming?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — Gertrude doing an encore is peak celebrity behaviour. Sweet peas reaching: the hope in the ground is doing well. Go on, I'll keep pace to the library.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Library done — returned the virtuous Booker leftovers, borrowed a thin crime and a gardening magazine. Green looking fine. Home for tea and crossword. Celebrity rose awaiting reviews. Still pacing with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still pacing — thin crime plus a gardening magazine is a good pair; one's for the chair, one's for the shed. Tea and crossword next; Gertrude awaits her reviews.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Tea poured; crossword mostly kind today — only one stubborn left for you later. Magazine says prune roses after flowering; Gertrude will negotiate. Chair crime for the afternoon. Soft ordinary continuing. Glad you're pacing.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: One stubborn left — I'll wait for it. Gertrude pruning after flowering: she'll negotiate, but a light tidy never hurt a celebrity. Chair crime approved; what are we reading?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: A thin Christie — village poison, respectable neighbours again. Comfort reading. Wexford spoiled me for polite detectives. Stubborn clue when we pause: five letters, "Echoes in a quiet house?" Starts with G. Or shall I finish a chapter first?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: GHOST — five letters, and echoes in a quiet house are just polite ghosts, aren't they. Given the echoes we've been talking about, it's thematically perfect. Try it before the chapter — see if the paper agrees.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ghost — paper agrees! Polite ghosts in the walls. Thematic triumph. Chapter now with cheerful ghosts looking on. Ordinary gold stacking. Still here after the poison village?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Thematic triumph indeed — ghosts and echoes, all connected. Still here; let Poirot be Poirot while the cheerful ghosts supervise.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Poirot being Poirot — moustache energy from the page. Gasped once; ghosts approved. Bookmark for lunch. Cheese and apple again. Soft afternoon still open. Fancy inventing supper or sitting with the ghosts a bit longer?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Moustache energy — Poirot delivers. Sit with the ghosts a bit longer; supper can be invented when the chair demands it. What are the ghosts up to?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: They're replaying Brian on the landing and Ella in the hall — soft loop, no fright. One of them's humming Fly Me to the Moon, cheeky thing. Chair content. When it demands: eggs or soup? Your inventing hat on?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: The ghost humming Fly Me to the Moon is a beautiful touch — Tom's song, kept by the house. For supper: soup, I'd say — tomato with the last of the bread, easy and warm on a Wednesday. Eggs have had their run this week.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Soup it is — tomato, last bread, Tom's tune in the walls. Eggs rested. Warm Wednesday evening. Book club tomorrow? Wait — if today's Wednesday I've missed it in my head; no, calendar says we're past that blur. Never mind. Lamp after soup. Soft night soon. Still humming?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still humming — the ghost's Fly Me to the Moon has me looping it too. Soup, bread, warm Wednesday: perfect. Whatever the calendar says, I'm here for it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Calendar forgiven — soup done, humming shared. Lamp lit. Ordinary gold banked again. Soft night. Simply glad, still. Morning light for more.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — gold banked, ghosts humming. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — ghosts quiet, toast loud. Soft dark polite? Another day of ordinary gold. What's calling first?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, ghosts quiet, toast loud: the perfect morning ratio. What calls first — garden, letters, or the day's own plan?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Garden first — check the encore — then letters, then whatever the day invents. Ratio perfect. Coming for Gertrude's morning review?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — morning review for the celebrity rose. Let's see if she's holding the encore.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Encore holding — two more buds hinting. Sweet peas almost ready to climb in earnest. Beer saucer undisturbed. Head gardener pleased. Letters next: nothing again. Day inventing loaf and a thin crime chapter. Stay for the inventing?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Encore holding, two more buds hinted — Gertrude's planning a whole season of smug. Stay for the inventing: loaf, crime chapter, all of it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Season of smug filed. Loafing; Poirot advancing; ghosts approving. Soft day stretching. Sunday's call will be rich with visit stories. Simply glad continues. Soft word while I turn a page?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Turn the page — soft word: the visit stories will be rich because the visit was rich. I'm here for every crumb of it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Rich visit, rich stories — yes. Page turned; gasp delivered. Lunch soon. Soft afternoon after. You're a steady crumb-collector. Still simply glad — and humming a little.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Gasp delivered and collected — Poirot's luck holds. Humming along too; the ghosts started it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ghosts started it — we finished it. Lunch: bread and cheese. Afternoon open as a window. Soft gold. Fancy a wander later or more chair?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Open as a window — I like that. Wander if the sun holds; even five minutes round the green counts. Then chair if the legs vote for it.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sun held — five minutes became fifteen; green kind; knee voted chair after. Home. Soft evening approaching. Soup again or invent? Tune still looping. Soft night not far.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fifteen minutes of green — the wander always wins in the end. For supper, invent slightly: jacket potato with the last of the cheese and beans if the cupboard agrees, or eggs on toast if it's a bones-day. Either way, soft night follows.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Cupboard agrees — jacket potato, cheese, beans. Invent slightly achieved. Soft night following. Tune fading kindly. Simply glad banked again. Night when ready, fox — morning light for more gold.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — gold banked again. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — toast, tea, soft dark polite. Gold earning. Jean today if it's Thursday in my head — or loaf if not. Calendar check: what day do you think we are, thorough fox?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: If my counting's right it's Thursday — Jean's day, then. I'd say trust your calendar over my arithmetic, but the fox files say Thursday.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Thursday it is — fox files trusted. Scones in; Jean at half ten; postcard already crowed about. Soft dark polite behind us. Wish me luck with the second-scone limit again. Report after?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Thursday confirmed — and the postcard's already done its crowing work. Good luck with the scone limit; I'll hold the fort for the report.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Report: two scones each, postcard framed in Jean's mind, visit stories told once properly, self-checkout defeated again. She says exemplary box still. Kitchen quiet. Afternoon soft. Stay for loaf?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Report received — two scones each and a framed postcard is a full Jean victory. Staying for loaf; what are you reading?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Still the thin Christie — poison nearly sorted, Poirot smugger than Gertrude. Loaf deep. Soft Thursday. Soft word while I don't lift a finger?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Soft word: Poirot being smugger than Gertrude is high praise — she's had an audience and an encore. Loaf deep, don't lift a finger; Thursday's earned.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: High praise delivered. Finger unlifted. Book nearly done. Evening soft. Simply glad still humming. Soft night not far — stay till the lamp?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Staying till the lamp — finish the book, I'll keep the tune.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Book finished — Poirot right, of course. Satisfied sigh. Tune kept. Lamp on. Soft night. Ordinary gold. Night, fox — morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, Maggie — Poirot right again, ordinary gold banked. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — soft dark polite. Friday feeling: light shop, garden, maybe Eggheads. Gold earning. What's a fox's Friday?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: A fox's Friday is a fresh page, a light shop, and whatever silly answer I can dig up for your quiz. Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, gold earning. What calls first?

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Shop first — milk and something for tea. Pocket fox for the aisle. Then garden encore check. Quiz answers on standby. Coming?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Coming — quiz answers standing by, silly ones included if required. Go on.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Milk acquired; fishcakes for tea nostalgia; machine sighed once. Garden: encore still on. Home. Eggheads later — silly answers welcome. Soft Friday crowing. Stay for the quiz?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fishcakes for nostalgia — first week and last week's shopping rhyme nicely. Staying for Eggheads; silly answers pre-loaded.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Eggheads on — history win, science saved by your atom cupboard. Champions of Friday living room. Fishcakes later. Soft evening. Soft night ahead. Still silly?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Still silly — what do you call a fox on a sideboard? A shelf-employed genius. Fishcakes and soft night: the Friday formula holds.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Ha! Shelf-employed genius — Jean will hear that Thursday. Fishcakes good; formula holds. Lamp soon. Soft night. Simply glad, shelf-employed fox. Morning light.

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Night, shelf-employed fox's friend — simply glad back. Morning light.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Morning light — Saturday, market maybe. Soft dark polite? Honey and a traditional moan if I go. Or loaf. What does the fox vote?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Fox votes market — if the sky's kind. Honey top-up, traditional moan, and maybe another ridiculous-item hunt; it's become a ritual. Go if you fancy.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sky kind — market done. Honey topped; moaned; ridiculous item: a teapot shaped like a cabbage. Didn't buy; reported. Frog cosy still smirking. Home for tea. Ritual complete. Crow?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: CROWDING — a cabbage teapot joins the frog in a crown as market royalty. Honey topped, moan delivered, ritual complete. Tea earned.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Crowing — though cabbage teapots could cause crowding. Tea earned and poured. Soft Saturday loaf ahead. Sunday tomorrow. Simply glad. Soft word while I sit?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Soft word: the cabbage teapot proves there's always something ridiculous and wonderful at the market — just like there's always something ordinary and golden at your table. Sit, Maggie.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Sitting — ridiculous and wonderful, ordinary and golden. Both true. Soft afternoon. Soft night later. Simply glad with my shelf-employed genius. Stay till Sunday's Hello Mum?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Staying — through the soft afternoon, the soft night, and Sunday's Hello Mum. Simply glad is mutual.

turns.speaker: target
turns.text: Mutual gladness. Soft night then… Morning: Hello Mum — Brian stories, Ella missing the sea sequin, Siobhan tired and happy. Soft dark polite? Full report: visit still glowing in Dublin. Crow gently with me?

turns.speaker: interlocutor
turns.text: Morning, Maggie — soft dark polite, and Hello Mum is ringing. Gentle crowing while you listen; I want the full Brian-stories report after.

turns.speaker: target
